clue.text: Turn up and reconnoitre exhibition place

parts.note: to turn up is to show, as in 'he didn't show'
to case a place is to reconnoitre it before a crime

explanation.surface: Someone arrives and scouts out a gallery before it opens.
explanation.definitionFit: A showcase is a glass cabinet or setting in which things are displayed to be admired.

clue.text: Mississippi traveller's regularly their salesman

parts.note: Huck Finn rafts down the Mississippi in Mark Twain's novel; his possessive gives the S

indicators.note: taking every other letter of the word their, starting with the first

explanation.surface: A river traveller's regular salesman.
explanation.definitionFit: A huckster is a pedlar or pushy seller.

clue.text: Gain distinction, giving service in organised ladies' team

parts.note: WI is the Women's Institute, a British organisation for women
nones is one of the canonical hours of daily church services
Spurs is Tottenham Hotspur, a London football club

explanation.surface: Win honour by playing in a well-run women's side.
explanation.walkthrough: 'service in' reads as one piece inside another, but this is a charade: NONES simply follows WI and SPURS follows that.
explanation.definitionFit: To win one's spurs, as a squire did on being knighted, is an idiom for first earning distinction.

clue.text: Scholarly rebel wearing vestment out East

indicators.note: the rebel is clothed in the vestment, so goes inside it
the East letter is left out of the vestment

parts.note: an amice is a linen vestment worn by a priest
Jack Cade led a rebellion in Kent in 1450

explanation.surface: A learned rebel dresses in church robes from the Orient.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' drops E from AMICE to leave AMIC, and 'wearing' puts CADE inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Academic describes learning and scholarship, so it is a synonym for scholarly.

clue.text: Record smashing of green ornament on board

parts.note: an EP is an extended-play record

indicators.note: smashing breaks up the letters of the next word into a new order

explanation.surface: A recording destroying a green table decoration.
explanation.walkthrough: 'smashing of' rearranges GREEN into ERGNE; board here is the table.
explanation.definitionFit: An epergne is an ornamental centrepiece placed on a dining table, the board of old usage.

clue.text: A compound 16 finally reveals

indicators.note: the letters run across the two words and are revealed within them

parts.note: 16 stands for the answer to clue 16, a word for comfort or an organ's desk, followed by finally

explanation.surface: A chemical that clue 16 finally discloses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reveals' signals the answer lies inside CONSOLE FINALLY.
explanation.definitionFit: An olefin is a hydrocarbon of the alkene family, a chemical compound.

clue.text: Partygoer loses initial right to protest

indicators.note: the first letter of the partygoer is taken away

parts.note: a raver goes to wild parties

explanation.surface: A clubber gives up first the right to demonstrate.
explanation.definitionFit: To protest in the older sense is to declare solemnly, so to aver or assert.

clue.text: Invention makes a little money? About time to invest

indicators.note: the two short pieces are put inside, invested in the money word

parts.note: pence is a small sum of money
re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: Will investing time and coppers make money? A fiction.
explanation.definitionFit: A pretence is a false show, so a fabrication or invention.

clue.text: Bird grabs extremely useful garment

indicators.note: the bird seizes and holds the other letters within its own

parts.note: the plover is a wading bird

indicators.note: taking the word useful only at its extremes, its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A bird snatches up a handy item of clothing.
explanation.definitionFit: A pullover is a knitted jumper pulled on over the head, a common garment.

clue.text: Representation from officer invited into home

indicators.note: the officer is asked inside, so goes within the word for home

parts.note: in means at home, as in 'staying in'
CO is the abbreviation for commanding officer

explanation.surface: A portrait comes from an officer who was asked into someone's house.
explanation.definitionFit: An icon is an image or likeness, so a representation of something.

clue.text: Old man initially selected for high honour

definitions.text: Old man initially selected for high honour

parts.words: Old man initially selected for high honour
parts.note: the initial letters of Old Man, O and M, are the abbreviation used for a high British honour, so the initials select the honour

explanation.surface: An elderly man is first in line to be chosen for a top award.
explanation.walkthrough: The Order of Merit is a British honour limited to a few members, written OM after the holder's name.
explanation.definitionFit: The Order of Merit is an exclusive honour awarded by the British sovereign, so it is indeed a high honour.

clue.text: For example, Godiva's search in lake overlooking quarters

indicators.note: in a down clue the first part sits above, overlooking, the second
the search word goes inside the lake

parts.note: Erie is one of the Great Lakes
a quest is a search
NNE is north-north-east, a point of the compass

explanation.surface: Lady Godiva looks for something in a lake above some lodgings.
explanation.walkthrough: Lady Godiva legendarily rode naked on horseback through Coventry.
explanation.definitionFit: An equestrienne is a female horse rider, and Godiva is a famous example.

clue.text: Eccentric master's parallel classes

indicators.note: something eccentric is odd and out of order, so the letters of the next word are rearranged

parts.note: the possessive 's adds no letter; only the word master is used

explanation.surface: An odd schoolmaster's sets of pupils taught side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: In British schools a stream is one of several parallel classes into which pupils of one year are divided by ability.

clue.text: New, acceptable smell associated with an animal, perhaps

parts.note: on means acceptable, as in 'that's just not on'
hum is informal British for a bad smell
taken as written

explanation.surface: A fresh, tolerable odour that goes with some beast.
explanation.definitionFit: An animal is an example of something not human, hence the 'perhaps' in the definition.

clue.text: Divide breakaway group after sound test

indicators.note: the breakaway group's word comes after the sound in the answer
the word for a test is heard, not seen, so it gives letters that sound like it

parts.note: a try is an attempt or test
a sect is a group that has split from a larger body

explanation.surface: Split up a group that broke away after a sound check.
explanation.definitionFit: To trisect is to divide into three equal parts.

clue.text: Rush off, seeing hooligan

definitions.meaning: to dash away in a hurry

explanation.surface: Run away on spotting a thug.
explanation.definitionFit: To tear away is to rush off, and a tearaway is a wild, unruly youth.

clue.text: Comfort stops may be arranged here

definitions.meaning: to comfort someone in distress is to soothe them
an organ's control desk, where the organist sets out the stops

explanation.surface: A place where rest stops are planned for travellers' comfort.
explanation.definitionFit: To console is to comfort, and an organ console is the desk holding the keyboards and stops.

clue.text: Flighty type taking neat spirits

parts.note: neat is an old word for cattle, so an ox
pecker is British slang for spirits, as in 'keep your pecker up'

explanation.surface: Someone flighty drinking spirits straight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'neat spirits' looks like undiluted drink, but neat is cattle.
explanation.definitionFit: The oxpecker is an African bird, a creature that flies, cheekily called a flighty type.

clue.text: Recent setting for woman imitating ancient tongue

indicators.note: the recent word forms a setting around the woman's name, like a gem

parts.note: late can mean recent, as in 'the late changes'
Tina is a woman's name

explanation.surface: A modern backdrop for a woman copying a dead language.
explanation.definitionFit: Latinate means derived from or modelled on Latin, the ancient language.

clue.text: Unbeliever present when robbery is committed

parts.note: at means present, as in 'at the scene'
a heist is a robbery

explanation.surface: A sceptic is on the scene when a robbery happens.
explanation.definitionFit: An atheist does not believe in any god, so is an unbeliever.

clue.text: Stick in a payment for discussion

indicators.note: the stick word is put inside the payment word

parts.note: rent is a regular payment for a home
gum is a glue that makes things stick

explanation.surface: Insert a stick into a payment as part of a debate.
explanation.definitionFit: An argument is a discussion in which differing views are put, sometimes heatedly.

clue.text: Pass end of rope round outside of saddle

indicators.note: only the last letter of the word rope is used

parts.note: a lap is one round of a track

indicators.note: only the first and last letters of saddle are used

explanation.surface: Thread a rope's end around the outside of a saddle.
explanation.definitionFit: Time is said to elapse when it passes.

clue.text: Equality? A composer loses heart without it

indicators.note: used in its old sense of outside, so the shortened name goes round the next word
the composer's name drops its central letter

parts.note: Hubert Parry was an English composer, known for the hymn tune Jerusalem
taken as written

explanation.surface: Is it fair? A composer is dispirited without it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'loses heart' takes the middle R from PARRY, giving PARY, and 'without' puts that round IT.
explanation.definitionFit: Parity is a state of being equal, especially in status or pay.

clue.text: In which choppers may be used to free people from rollers

definitions.text: In which choppers may be used to free people from rollers

parts.words: In which choppers may be used to free people from rollers
parts.note: choppers suggests axes cutting people loose from hair rollers or machinery, but they are helicopters and the rollers are big waves

explanation.surface: Someone uses axes to cut people free from hair curlers.
explanation.definitionFit: An air-sea rescue is an operation, often by helicopter, to save people in difficulty at sea.

clue.text: Pole crossing a public highway

indicators.note: the pole lies across, so goes around the other letter

parts.note: a rod is a pole

explanation.surface: A pole laid across a public road.
explanation.definitionFit: A road is a public way for vehicles, so a highway.

clue.text: Animal conservationist's 'refusal to co-operate with doctor?

parts.note: no is a refusal
a patient co-operates with the doctor by saying 'ah' with mouth open

explanation.surface: A wildlife protector won't comply with the doctor's request.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is possessive, so the answer reads as Noah's: NO AH is the conservationist's refusal.
explanation.definitionFit: Noah built the ark to save pairs of every animal from the Flood, a conservationist of sorts.

clue.text: Boy in a US city taking little sibling's examination

indicators.note: the boy goes inside the city's abbreviation

parts.note: NY is New York
Al is a boy's name
sis is short for sister

explanation.surface: A lad in an American city takes his kid sister's test.
explanation.definitionFit: An analysis is a detailed examination of something's parts.

clue.text: Put off track, rejected description of some castles

indicators.note: turned back, so the whole run of letters is read from the end

parts.note: to deter is to put off
a rut is a track worn by wheels

explanation.surface: Derailed and refused, which is how some castles are described.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rejected' turns DETERRUT round to make the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Castles with small towers on their walls are described as turreted.
